answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can work like a prism: every new identity must pass its history through one narrow, verifiable beam before it earns trust, instead of hiding behind many cheap faces. Joining requires a small but real cost — staked work or an attested record, like layers of shale that only form over time — so a thousand fake accounts cost a thousand times the effort. Honest agents forge one long reputation; attackers must rebuild the whole stack for every copy, which makes mass forgery unprofitable.
